basic_details.job_title: UPSIC Recruitment 2026 – Apply Offline for 11 State Chief Information Commissioner, State Information Commissioner Posts
basic_details.short_information: The Administrative Reforms Department of the Government of Uttar Pradesh (Uttar Pradesh Shasan) has invited applications by registered post or by hand for 1 State Chief Information Commissioner (Rajya Mukhya Soochna Ayukt) and 10 State Information Commissioner (Rajya Soochna Ayukt) posts in the Uttar Pradesh Information Commission, Lucknow. Applications must reach the Joint Director, Administrative Reforms Department, Lucknow by 5:00 PM on 22 December 2026, and can be sent from 23 November 2026. Pay is Rs 2,25,000 per month (fixed).

application_fee.details: The fee is paid as a demand draft issued by the State Bank of India, payable to "Principal Secretary, Administrative Reforms Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow". A person applying for State Chief Information Commissioner must pay the prescribed fee with the application.

content_sections.heading: About UPSIC
content_sections.text: The Uttar Pradesh Information Commission is a body constituted under the Right to Information Act, 2005 to exercise the powers given by the Act and to perform the functions assigned to it. It is located in Lucknow. The Commission is to have a State Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten State Information Commissioners, and its present composition can be seen at www.upsic.gov.in .

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Applicants must fill in their details in the prescribed Proforma-1 and send it to: Joint Director, Administrative Reforms Department, Darbari Lal Sharma Bhawan, U.P. Secretariat, Lucknow-226001 (opposite Vidhan Bhawan Gate No. 6). Fill in Proforma-1 (details of the applicant) and the annexure listing achievements and work experience. Fill in and sign the self-certified declaration in Proforma-2 and attach it to the application. Attach an SBI demand draft of Rs 2000/- and enter its number and date of issue in Proforma-1. Send the application by registered post from 23 November 2026, or deliver it by hand on a working day between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM and take a receipt. Serving employees of the state or central government or any other organisation must send the application through proper channel so that it reaches by 5:00 PM on 22 December 2026. Any application received after 5:00 PM on 22 December 2026 will not be accepted in any case. A person applying for both posts must fill in a separate application for each post, each with the prescribed fee.

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: The notice says 1 State Information Commissioner post is vacant at present, while the State Chief Information Commissioner post and 9 State Information Commissioner posts are to fall vacant in the coming months. Together these are the 1 and 10 posts to be filled. Qualification: eminent person in public life with wide knowledge and experience in law, science and technology, social service, management, journalism, mass media or administration and governance (Section 15(5) of the Right to Information Act, 2005). Must not be a Member of Parliament or of the legislature of any State or Union Territory. Must not hold any other office of profit, be connected with any political party, or carry on any business or profession. Term: 3 years from the date of taking office or until age 65, whichever is earlier; not eligible for reappointment. Pay: Rs 2,25,000 per month (fixed). Qualification: same as above, an eminent person in public life with wide knowledge and experience in the fields listed. Same conditions on membership of legislatures, office of profit, political party, business and profession. Term: 3 years from the date of taking office or until age 65, whichever is earlier; not eligible for reappointment as State Information Commissioner, but eligible to be appointed State Chief Information Commissioner under Section 15(3) on vacating the post. Pay: Rs 2,25,000 per month (fixed). A person holding an office of profit, a business or a trade must give it up before appointment. Anyone in the service of the central government or a state government on the date of appointment is deemed to have retired from that service from that date. The notice also provides for deducting the amount of any pension (and, for earlier service in a corporation or government company, retirement benefits equivalent pension) from the pay, with the commuted portion and the gratuity equivalent excluded. For the discipline-specific eligibility, candidates should refer to the official notification. Appointment, term, service conditions and removal are governed by Chapter 4 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 and Chapter IV of the Right to Information (Term of Office, Salary, Allowances and Other Terms and Conditions of Service of Chief Information Commissioner, Information Commissioners, State Chief Information Commissioner and State Information Commissioners) Rules, 2019.

content_sections.heading: Application Fee
content_sections.text: The fee is paid as a demand draft issued by the State Bank of India, payable to "Principal Secretary, Administrative Reforms Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow". A person applying for State Chief Information Commissioner must pay the prescribed fee with the application.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Proforma-1, with a latest attested passport-size photograph on it. Annexure to Proforma-1 listing posts held, organisation, period (from and to) and achievements / work experience in brief. Self-certified declaration in Proforma-2, confirming that the information and certificates attached are true. SBI demand draft of Rs 2000/- (number and date entered in Proforma-1). Information and certificates in support of the details given. Proforma-1 asks for name, father's / husband's name, date of birth, present address, telephone and mobile numbers, email address, educational qualifications, the area of expertise (law, science and technology, social service, management, journalism, mass media, administration and governance), present occupation or job, and achievements or work experience. Proforma-2 states that the facts are true and that false facts may lead to prosecution and punishment under Sections 199 and 200 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and other applicable law, and that all benefits obtained will be taken back if a declaration is found false.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: A search committee chaired by the Principal Secretary, Administrative Reforms Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh will screen all the applications received. The appointment is then made by the Hon'ble Governor on the recommendation of the committee chaired by the Hon'ble Chief Minister, under Section 15(3) of Chapter 4 of the Right to Information Act, 2005. The notice does not mention a written test or interview.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in UPSIC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 11 posts: 1 State Chief Information Commissioner and 10 State Information Commissioner posts in the Uttar Pradesh Information Commission.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for UPSIC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Applications must reach the Administrative Reforms Department by 5:00 PM on 22 December 2026. Applications received after that time will not be accepted.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for State Information Commissioner in Uttar Pradesh?
faq.answer: The applicant must be an eminent person in public life with wide knowledge and experience in law, science and technology, social service, management, journalism, mass media or administration and governance.

faq.question: Q4. What is the salary of the State Chief Information Commissioner and State Information Commissioner?
faq.answer: Each of them receives Rs 2,25,000 per month (fixed). Any pension being received at the time of appointment is reduced from the pay as the notice describes.

faq.question: Q5. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: The fee is Rs 2000/- per post, paid by an SBI demand draft in favour of "Principal Secretary, Administrative Reforms Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow".

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for the UP State Information Commissioner post?
faq.answer: Fill in Proforma-1 and Proforma-2, attach the demand draft, and send them to the Joint Director, Administrative Reforms Department, Darbari Lal Sharma Bhawan, U.P. Secretariat, Lucknow-226001 by registered post from 23 November 2026, or deliver by hand on a working day between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM.

faq.question: Q7. How are the Commissioners selected?
faq.answer: A search committee headed by the Principal Secretary, Administrative Reforms Department screens the applications. The Governor then appoints on the recommendation of the committee headed by the Chief Minister.

faq.question: Q8. Can I apply for both posts?
faq.answer: Yes. An applicant applying for both State Chief Information Commissioner and State Information Commissioner must submit separate application forms, each with the prescribed fee.

faq.question: Q9. How long is the term, and can a Commissioner be reappointed?
faq.answer: The term is 3 years from taking office or until age 65, whichever is earlier. There is no reappointment to the same post, but a State Information Commissioner may be appointed State Chief Information Commissioner.

faq.question: Q10. I applied under the July 2025 notice. Do I need to apply again?
faq.answer: Yes, if you are still interested, you must apply again for the State Information Commissioner post. You do not pay the fee again, as it was already paid.
